core_obligations: Algebra structure and the coefficient object (proof lines 1867-1898): the functor applied to motives gives a contravariant functor to graded vector spaces with a Kunneth isomorphism and a graded commutative algebra structure via the diagonal, and the invertibility of the value on the twist together with the degree assumption allows choosing compatible isomorphisms identifying the twists of the coefficients with shifted copies of the coefficient field.

Cycle class and degree map (proof lines 1898-1916): correspondence groups from the base to a variety are rational Chow groups, so applying the functor produces the cycle class map into the cohomology; the class of the fundamental cycle gives a morphism from the twisted motive to the unit whose image under the functor in degree zero is the degree map.

The axioms (proof lines 1916-2027): duality of the twisted motive gives finiteness and nondegenerate pairings, which proves parts (a) and (b) of the axiom on duality; monoidality gives the axiom on products and the base field; compatibility of the cycle class map with pullbacks, the projection formula, compatibility with exterior products and the behaviour of the class of the base follow from the correspondence description and the duality preparation lemma.
proof_roadmap: Construct the algebra structure and identify the twists of the coefficients.
Produce the cycle class map and the degree map from correspondence groups.
Verify the duality, product and functoriality axioms.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that over an algebraically closed field a rational linear monoidal functor from motives to graded vector spaces whose value on the twist is concentrated in degree minus two produces data (D1), (D2) and (D3) satisfying all the axioms of a Weil cohomology theory except possibly two parts of the duality axiom (statement lines 1857-1866). The proof (proof lines 1867-2027) constructs the algebra, the cycle class map and the degree map and verifies the axioms through duality of motives, monoidality and correspondences. H3: a long construction with an axiom by axiom verification, written out in full.
